blocks.en: Abstract
blocks.zh: 摘要

blocks.en: Reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards (RLVR) produces rich training experience, yet outcome rewards reduce each attempt to a single number and leave most of this information unused. Training-time scaffolds, such as strategies or hints added to the prompt during training, offer a natural way to turn this information into guidance, but their design and adaptation are largely left to humans and tailored to specific domains. We introduce AutoScaffold, a unified AI-for-AI framework that turns a student's training experience into adaptive scaffolds, with minimal domain-specific information and no human intervention during training. A frozen teacher periodically examines this experience, diagnoses bottlenecks, and designs scaffolds in two forms: (i) strategies shared across a class of tasks and (ii) hints for individual hard tasks, adjusting the content and amount of support as the student learns. The scaffolds are removed at evaluation. We apply the same framework to ALFWorld, search-based QA, mathematical reasoning, and GPU kernel generation. When evaluated without scaffolds, students trained with AutoScaffold outperform those trained with the corresponding RL baselines in all four domains, with gains of 7.2 points in ALFWorld success and 4.0 points in average QA exact match. On GPU kernel generation, AutoScaffold increases the fraction of tasks with a correct kernel that runs faster than the PyTorch reference by up to 5.0 points. On math, our student surpasses QuestA's reported accuracy using approximately one-third as many student training steps. Analyses show that the teacher identifies a different failure in each task class and shifts its scaffolds from step-by-step workflows to targeted fixes as the student improves, and that its revised scaffolds help the student learn more than keeping the previous scaffold or using no scaffold.
blocks.zh: 以可核查奖励(RLVR)加强学习可产生丰富的培训经验,但成果奖励将每次尝试减少到一个数字并留下大部分这些信息被使用. 培训时间脚手架,如在培训期间添加到提示的策略或提示,提供了将这些信息转化为指导的自然方式,但其设计和适应性基本上留给人类,并适合特定领域. 我们引入了AutoScaffold,一个统一的AI-for-AI框架,将学生的训练经验转化为适应性脚手架,在训练期间只有最少的域特有信息,没有人类干预. 被冻结的教师定期检查这一经验,诊断出瓶颈,并以两种形式设计脚手架:(一) 在一个类别的任务中共享战略;和(二) 个别艰苦任务的提示,随着学生的学习,调整支持的内容和数量. 脚手架在评审时被删除. 我们对ALFWorld,基于搜索的QA,数学推理,以及GPU内核生成应用了相同的框架. 在没有脚手架的情况下进行评价时,接受自动脚手架培训的学生在所有四个领域都超过了接受相应RL基线培训的学生,获得的ALFWorld成功7.2分,平均QA精确比分4.0分. 在GPU内核生成上,AutoScaffold会将运行速度快于PyTorch参考数的正确内核任务分数增加至5.0分. 在数学方面,我们的学生使用大约三分之一的学生培训步骤,超过了QuestA报告的准确性. 分析显示,教师在每个任务班级中都识别出不同的失败,并随着学生的改善而将脚手架从分步工作流程转向定向固定,其修改后脚手架比保留之前的脚手架或使用没有脚手架更能帮助学生学习.

blocks.en: 1 Introduction
blocks.zh: 导言

blocks.en: Reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards (RLVR) has become a standard approach to post-training language models for reasoning and agentic tasks ( Shao et al., 2024 ; Yu et al., 2025 ; Feng et al., 2025 ) . Every training step produces rich experience: the model’s reasoning, its actions, and the feedback it receives. Yet RL learns from this experience only through outcome rewards, which reduce each rollout to a single number. Much of what the rollouts reveal is lost: a failed attempt may contain useful reasoning or actions, a successful one may rely on an inefficient strategy, and on tasks that are too hard for the model, nearly every attempt fails and the reward provides no signal at all (Appendix A ). Making better use of training experience is therefore an opportunity to improve post-training beyond what rewards alone can teach.
blocks.zh: 强化有可核查奖励的学习(RLVR)已经成为培养后语言模型用于推理和代理任务的标准方法(Shao等,2024;Yu等,2025;Feng等,2025)。 每个培训步骤都产生丰富的经验:模型的推理、其行动以及收到的反馈。 然而,RL只能通过结果奖励来从这一经验中吸取教训,结果奖励将每次推出都减少到一个数字. 推展所揭示的大部分都丢失了:失败的尝试可能包含有用的推理或行动,成功的尝试可能依赖于效率低下的战略,而对于模型来说过于困难的任务,几乎每一次尝试都失败了,而奖励根本就没有信号(附录A. 因此,更好地利用培训经验是一个机会,可以改进后培训,而不只是奖励。

blocks.en: One promising way to turn such experience into guidance is training-time scaffolding , which refers to the procedure of adding auxiliary text (a scaffold ), such as a strategy, hint, or partial solution, to the prompt of the model being trained (the student ) ( Zhang et al., 2026 ; Li et al., 2026a ; Lu et al., 2026 ) . A scaffold conveys what the reward alone cannot: on tasks the student cannot yet solve, it helps the student succeed so that these tasks produce learning signal, and more generally it shows the student better ways to reason and act. Scaffolds serve only to help the student learn during training and are removed at evaluation, where the student must solve tasks on its own.
blocks.zh: 将这种经验转化为指导的一个有希望的方法是训练时间脚手架,它指的是添加辅助文本(脚手架)的程序,如策略,提示,或部分解决方案,以促使正在训练的模型(学生)(张等,2026;李等,2026a;吕等,2026.). 脚手架传达的是奖励本身无法做到的:在学生尚不能解决的任务上,它帮助学生成功,使这些任务产生学习信号,更一般地向学生展示更好的理性和行动方式. 脚手架只服务于帮助学生在训练期间学习,在评价时被移除,学生必须自己解决任务.

blocks.en: Existing scaffolding methods, however, fall short in three respects. First, most are not automatic and do not draw on the student’s training experience: their scaffolds are prepared before training, as hand-designed hint tiers, partial solutions, or predefined skills ( Zhang et al., 2026 ; Li et al., 2026a ; Lu et al., 2026 ) . A few methods derive support from the student’s training experience, distilling trajectories into skills or generating guidance from failed attempts ( Xia et al., 2026 ; He et al., 2026 ) , but they do so through fixed pipelines. Second, they are not fully adaptive . As the student learns, its abilities change: the failures a scaffold was designed for may disappear, and new failures appear that it does not address, so a scaffold that helped early in training may no longer help the student learn. Yet support either stays fixed or changes through predefined procedures: SAGE tunes hint strength with fixed rollout-based rules ( Liao et al., 2026 ) , Skill0 withdraws skills through a predefined staged curriculum ( Lu et al., 2026 ) , and SkillRL revises skills from a prescribed sample of failures without measuring their effect on the current student ( Xia et al., 2026 ) . Third, they are not unified : each is built around one task structure, such as hints or solution prefixes for mathematical reasoning or skill libraries for agentic tasks. A mathematical solution prefix, for example, does not provide the action sequencing or object-interaction strategies needed for an agentic task, so each new domain requires a new design. Deciding what support a domain needs, and how it should change over training, is therefore left to human researchers, who design scaffolds from their understanding of the domain and the model’s failures, often refining them across repeated training runs.
blocks.zh: 然而,现有的脚手架方法在三个方面还不足。 首先,大多数不是自动的,也不借鉴学生的训练经验:他们的脚手架是在训练前准备的,是手工设计的提示级,部分解决方案,或预先定义的技能(张等,2026;李等,2026a;吕等,2026). 少数方法从学生的训练经验中获得支持,将轨迹分解为技能,或从失败的尝试中产生指导(Xia等,2026;He等,2026),但都是通过固定管道完成的. 第二,它们不完全适应。 随着学生的学习,其能力会发生变化:一个脚手架所设计的失败可能会消失,而新的失败似乎并没有解决,因此一个早期帮助训练的脚手架可能不再帮助学生学习. 然而,支持要么保持固定,要么通过预先确定的程序进行修改: SAGE调用固定的推出规则来暗示力量(廖等,2026年),Skill0通过预设的分级课程来退出技能(卢等,2026年),SkillRL从规定的故障样本中修改技能而未测量其对当前学生的影响(夏等,2026年). 第三,它们并不统一 : 每个都围绕一个任务结构来构建,例如用于数学推理的提示或解决方案前缀或用于代理任务的技能库. 例如,数学解决方案前缀并不提供代理任务所需的动作测序或对象交互策略,因此每个新域都需要新的设计. 因此,决定一个领域需要什么支持,以及它应该如何改变培训,留给人类研究人员来决定,他们根据对这个领域和模型失败的理解来设计脚手架,常常通过反复的培训来完善它们。

blocks.en: These limitations motivate the central question of our work:
blocks.zh: 这些限制促使我们工作的核心问题是:

blocks.en: How can an LLM teacher turn a student’s training experience into scaffolds, designing and adapting them throughout RL post-training, across domains, without human intervention?
blocks.zh: 一个LLM教师怎么能将学生的训练经验变成脚手架,在RL的训练后,在不进行人类干预的情况下,设计和改造这些脚手架?

blocks.en: The difficulty is that the teacher’s ability to solve a task does not by itself tell it how to help a weaker, evolving student learn. Making scaffolding automatic , adaptive , and unified (Figure 2 a) poses three challenges. • Diagnosing the student’s bottlenecks. Aggregate rewards reveal whether the student succeeds, but not why it fails, while a few trajectories may not represent a whole task class; the teacher must decide which evidence to inspect and which failure patterns warrant intervention. • Choosing the right scaffold. The teacher must turn each diagnosis into a scaffold that suits the domain and targets either a weakness shared by a task class or a single hard task. The scaffold must also be of the right strength, because if it is too weak, every attempt may fail, and if it is too strong, every attempt may succeed. In particular, under binary outcome rewards, both cases yield identical rewards within a rollout group and no reward-based policy-gradient signal. A scaffold that is too strong can also let the student succeed without learning to solve the task on its own. • Validating and adapting scaffolds. A scaffold tailored to a few observed failures may not help the student solve other tasks in the same class, and a scaffold that helps at the current point can become unnecessary as the student improves. The teacher must assess proposed changes and decide when to revise or withdraw scaffolds, with the goal of improving the student’s performance without scaffolds.
blocks.zh: 困难在于,教师解决一项任务的能力本身并不能说明如何帮助一个弱小、不断发展的学生学习。 使脚手架自动、适应性和统一性(图2a)构成三个挑战。 二. 支助 分析学生瓶颈. 综合奖励揭示了学生是否成功,但并非其失败的原因,而一些轨迹可能不能代表整个任务班;教师必须决定哪些证据需要检查,哪些失败模式需要干预. 二. 支助 选取右脚手架. 老师必须将每个诊断转化为适合域的脚手架,并针对一个任务班共有的弱点或一个单一的艰巨任务. 脚手架也必须有正确的力量,因为如果太弱,每一个尝试都可能失败;如果太强,每一个尝试都可能成功. 特别是,在二进制结果奖励下,这两个案件在推出组内都得到同样的奖励,没有以奖励为基础的政策评级信号。 过于强壮的脚手架也可以让学生在没有学习自己解决任务的情况下成功. • 验证并调整脚手架。 适合少数被观察到的失败的脚手架可能无助于学生在同一班级解决其他任务,随着学生的改善,在目前阶段提供帮助的脚手架可能变得没有必要. 教师必须评估提议的修改,并决定何时修改或撤回脚手架,目的是提高学生的成绩,而不用脚手架。

blocks.en: Together, these challenges make obtaining effective scaffolds non-trivial, even with access to a strong teacher. They motivate a carefully designed framework that connects diagnosis, scaffold construction, and validation throughout training, so that the scaffold remains matched to the student’s evolving needs.

blocks.en: In this paper, we introduce AutoScaffold , a unified AI-for-AI framework in which a frozen teacher LLM observes an ongoing RL training run and automatically turns the student’s training experience into scaffolds injected into its training prompts (Figure AutoScaffold: AI-Guided Scaffolding for Reinforcement Learning of Language Models ). The approach draws on the educational principle of scaffolding: temporary, learner-contingent support that enables a learner to accomplish tasks beyond their current independent ability, and that is withdrawn as competence develops ( Wood et al., 1976 ; Vygotsky, 1978 ) . AutoScaffold automatically identifies the student’s bottlenecks and proposes new scaffolds. Every K K training steps the teacher investigates the student’s experience, using query tools to choose among training statistics, individual trajectories, groups of attempts on the same task, and its own past decisions (Figure 3 ). To choose the right scaffold, it diagnoses why the student fails and writes two levels of scaffold: class-level strategies shared across a task class, and instance-level hints for tasks the student cannot yet solve, which play complementary roles in our analysis (Appendix A ). Further, AutoScaffold also adaptively changes the content and strength of the scaffold based on the student’s current capability. The teacher revises the scaffolds every K K steps, and before deployment each class-level edit is validated on held-out tasks against no scaffold and the current scaffold, and the teacher uses these results to decide which edits to keep. It also revises how often class-level scaffolds are injected, and training with the updated scaffolds produces new experience for the next update. Finally, AutoScaffold unifies the design of the scaffold mechanism across a wide spectrum of application domains, requiring minimal domain-specific input such as the task description and the task classes at the beginning of the training.
blocks.zh: 校对:Soup 这种方法借鉴了脚手架的教育原则:提供临时、学习者-特遣队支助,使学习者能够完成超出其目前独立能力的任务,随着能力的发展而撤销(Wood等人,1976年;Vygotsky,1978年)。 AutoScaffold自动识别学生的瓶颈并提议新的脚手架. 每个KK培训步骤都由老师调查学生的经验,使用查询工具在培训统计、个人轨迹、相同任务的尝试组以及其自身过去的决定中进行选择(图3)。 要选择正确的脚手架,它会诊断学生为何失败,并写出两个层次的脚手架:跨任务班级共享的班级策略,以及学生尚未能解决的任务的例级提示,这在我们的分析中起到互补的作用(附录A. 此外,AutoScaffold还根据学生目前的能力,适应性地改变脚手架的内容和强度. 老师每KK步会修改脚手架,在部署之前,每个班级的编辑会针对没有脚手架和当前脚手架的被搁置任务进行验证,老师使用这些结果来决定要保留哪个编辑. 它还修改了课级脚手架的注射频率,而与更新后脚手架的培训为下一次更新创造了新的经验. 最后,AutoScaffold统一了跨多个应用域的脚手架机制设计,需要最小的域特有输入,如任务描述和培训开始时的任务班.

blocks.en: We evaluate AutoScaffold on four domains with distinct task structures and RL algorithms: ALFWorld (embodied household tasks, GiGPO), search-based question answering (GiGPO), mathematical reasoning (GRPO and DAPO), and KernelBench (GPU kernel generation, rubric-based GRPO). Under scaffold-free evaluation, AutoScaffold improves over the corresponding RL baselines in every domain (Figure 2 b,c), by 7.2 points in success rate on ALFWorld, 4.0 points in average exact match on search-based QA, up to 2.0 points in average accuracy on mathematical reasoning, and 3.0 points in correctness on KernelBench, and is competitive with or surpasses methods that rely on human-designed scaffolding. On KernelBench, it also raises the fraction of tasks with a correct kernel that runs faster than the PyTorch reference by up to 5.0 points (Table 7 ). On mathematical reasoning, it surpasses QuestA with approximately one-third as many student training steps. Ablations show the value of interactive queries and scaffold validation, and analyses of scaffold evolution show that, given only the general principles of scaffolding, the teacher decides on its own what scaffold to give, to which tasks, and how much, and revises these decisions as the student learns (Figure 2 d).
blocks.zh: 我们在四个任务结构和RL算法不同的领域评价AutoScaffold:ALFWorld(健美的家庭任务,GIGPO),基于搜索的问答(GiGPO),数学推理(GRPO和DAPO)和Kernel Bench(GPU内核生成,基于Rubic的GRPO). 在无脚手架评价下,AutoScaffold比每个域中相应的RL基线(图2b,c)提高,在ALFWorld上成功率为7.2分,在基于搜索的QA上平均准确匹配率为4.0分,在数学推理上平均准确度可达2.0分,在Kernel Bench上正确度可达3.0分,并且与依靠人设计的脚手架的方法具有竞争力或超越了这些方法. 在Kernel Bench上,它还用一个正确的内核提升了任务分数,这个内核运行速度快于PyTorch参考,最高可达5.0分(表7. 在数学推理方面,它以大约三分之一的学生培训步骤超过了QuestA. 分解显示交互查询和脚手架验证的价值,对脚手架演化的分析显示,由于只有脚手架的通则,教师自己决定分出什么脚手架,分出什么任务,分多少,并在学生学习时修改这些决定(图2d).

blocks.en: Our main contributions are as follows: • Automatic, adaptive scaffolding across domains. We introduce AutoScaffold , a unified AI-for-AI framework that turns a student’s training experience into evolving scaffolds through a frozen teacher LLM. The same procedure operates across domains with minimal domain-specific information and no human intervention during training. • A design that makes the teacher’s scaffolds effective. We design a framework that consists of a number of key components, such as adaptive scaffolding based on interactive queries and decision memory, controlled injection, and held-out validation of class-level revisions. Ablation studies show that each of these components is critical for the entire system; for example, removing scaffold validation reduces ALFWorld success by 14.1 points. • Principles for effective scaffolding. Under binary rewards, we characterize conditions under which class- and instance-level scaffolds strengthen group-relative learning signals, and show how overly strong scaffolds can eliminate these signals (Appendix A ). The analysis motivates combining strategies for shared weaknesses in a task class with hints for persistently unsolved tasks, and adapting support as the student learns. • Stronger performance without scaffolds. Across embodied tasks, search-based QA, mathematical reasoning, and GPU kernel generation, AutoScaffold improves over the corresponding RL baselines under scaffold-free evaluation and is competitive with or surpasses scaffolding methods that rely heavily on human design, without hand-written scaffolds or hand-designed schedules.

blocks.en: Automatic, adaptive scaffolding across domains. We introduce AutoScaffold , a unified AI-for-AI framework that turns a student’s training experience into evolving scaffolds through a frozen teacher LLM. The same procedure operates across domains with minimal domain-specific information and no human intervention during training.

blocks.en: 2 Related Work
blocks.zh: 2 相关工作

blocks.en: LLMs increasingly improve AI systems themselves, optimizing harnesses ( Lee et al., 2026 ) , writing GPU kernels ( Ouyang et al., 2025 ; Zhang et al., 2025b ) , and conducting parts of research ( Lu et al., 2024 ; Yamada et al., 2025 ; Karpathy, 2026 ) . For model training, LLMs have designed rewards ( Ma et al., 2024 ) , generated environments ( Chen et al., 2026a ) , and tuned hyperparameters ( Liu et al., 2025a ) , and PostTrainBench ( Rank et al., 2026 ) evaluates end-to-end automated post-training. Closest to our setting, LLMZero ( Fang et al., 2026 ) diagnoses training signals at each checkpoint and searches over hyperparameter transitions for GRPO, and EvoTrainer ( Chen et al., 2026b ) co-evolves the policy with a training-side harness by diagnosing rollouts and backtesting interventions. These methods operate on the training configuration or harness; AutoScaffold instead intervenes within a run at the level of task classes and instances, turning the student’s rollouts into guidance attached to its training prompts and removed at evaluation.
blocks.zh: LLMs日益改进人工智能系统本身,优化了用具(Lee等,2026年),撰写了GPU内核(Oyang等,2025年;Zhang等,2025年b)并进行了部分研究(Lu等,2024年;Yamada等,2025年;Karopathy,2026年)。 对于模式培训,LLMS设计了奖励(Ma等,2024年),生成了环境(Chen等,2026年a),并调制了超参数(Liu等,2025年a),以及PostTrain Bench(Rank等,2026年)评价了端到端的自动化后培训. EvoTrainer(Chen等,2026年b)通过诊断推开和反测试干预,将政策与培训侧管理结合起来。 这些方法运用于培训的配置或利用;AutoScaffold则在任务班级和实例一级的运行中进行干预,将学生的推广转化为培训的提示并被删除。

blocks.en: To address tasks on which nearly every rollout fails, known as the learning cliff ( Zhang et al., 2026 ) , prior work supplies task-specific hints, such as tiered hints in Scaf-GRPO ( Zhang et al., 2026 ) , partial solutions in QuestA ( Li et al., 2026a ) and POPE ( Qu et al., 2026 ) , stepwise hints in StepHint ( Zhang et al., 2025a ) , and self-generated hints in SAGE ( Liao et al., 2026 ) , or reusable skills for agentic tasks ( Xia et al., 2026 ; Lu et al., 2026 ; Lin et al., 2026a ; He et al., 2026 ; Shen et al., 2026 ) . In most methods, the form of guidance is designed by hand for one domain, and any adaptation follows predefined rules. The closest methods are SAGE, which adjusts hint strength with rollout-based rules; SkillRL, whose teacher revises skills from a fixed sample of failures without measuring their effect; and SLIM ( Shen et al., 2026 ) , which retains, retires, or adds skills by leave-one-skill-out validation but keeps some skills at inference. In contrast, AutoScaffold lets a frozen teacher choose which evidence to inspect, applies one procedure across domains, including math and GPU kernel generation, and validates class-level proposals on the current student before deployment. Table 1 positions AutoScaffold relative to both lines of work.
blocks.zh: 为了处理几乎每次推出都失败的任务,被称为"学习悬崖"(Zhang等,2026年),先前的工作提供了特定任务提示,如"Scaf-GRPO"(Zhang等,2026年)中的分级提示,"QuestA"(Li等,2026年a)和"POPE"(Qu等,2026年)中的部分解决方案,"StepHint"(Zhang等,2025年a)中的分步提示,"SAGE"(Lia等,2026年a)中的自发提示,"或可重复使用的干线任务技能"(Xia等,2026年;Lu等,2026年;Lin等,2026年a;He等,2026年;Shen等,2026年). 在大多数方法中,指向形式是用手为一个领域设计的,任何适应都遵循预先定义的规则. 最接近的方法有:SAGE,通过推出规则来调整提示强度;SkillRL,其老师从固定的故障样本中修改技能而未测量其效果;SLIM(沈等,2026年),通过休假一技能验证保留,退休,或增加技能,但保留一些技能推论. 相比之下,AutoScaffold让被冻结的老师选择检查哪些证据,在数学和GPU内核生成等多个领域应用一个程序,并在部署前验证关于当前学生的班级建议. 表1 相对于两行工作的自动脚手架。

blocks.en: 3 AutoScaffold
blocks.zh: 3 个自动脚手架

blocks.en: As mentioned in the introduction, an ideal scaffolding framework should be automatic, adaptive, and unified. Each requirement places demands on AutoScaffold. Being automatic means that no human designs or reviews the scaffolds, so the teacher must find out on its own why the student fails, write the scaffolds itself, and check its own proposals before using them. Being adaptive means that the scaffold must follow the current student, so it is revised throughout training, its effect is tracked across updates, and support is withdrawn once the student no longer needs it. Being unified means that the same procedure must apply to any domain, so it relies only on minimal domain-specific information, allows different forms of textual scaffold across domains, leaves the RL algorithm unchanged, and guides the teacher with principles from our analysis rather than domain-specific rules. Figure 3 gives an overview of AutoScaffold. We describe how the student is trained with scaffolds (Section 3.1 ) and how a frozen teacher LLM designs them every K K training steps (Section 3.2 ), noting which requirement each design serves.
blocks.zh: 如导言所提到,理想的脚手架框架应该是自动的、适应的和统一的。 每项要求都对自动脚手架提出了要求。 自动意味着没有人类的设计或审查脚手架,因此老师必须自己找出学生失败的原因,自己写脚手架,在使用脚手架之前先检查自己的提议. 适应性意味着脚手架必须跟随当下的学生,因此在整个培训过程中都会被修改,其效果会通过更新来跟踪,一旦学生不再需要支持,就撤回支持. 统一意味着同一程序必须适用于任何域,因此它只依靠最小的域特有信息,允许不同形式的跨域文字脚手架,使RL算法保持不变,并以我们分析的原则而不是域特有规则指导老师. 图3概括了"自动脚手架". 我们描述学生如何用脚手架培训(第3.1节),以及冷冻的教师如何设计每K K个培训步骤(第3.2节),指出每个设计都满足哪些要求。

blocks.en: This subsection explains why scaffolds help group-relative learning and why they must adapt to the student, defines scaffolds at two levels, and describes how they are injected into training prompts.

Whether the model learns from a given task therefore depends on whether its rollout group contains mixed outcomes ( Liao et al., 2026 ) . If each rollout succeeds independently with probability p p , then a mixed-outcome group occurs with probability u ⁡ ( p ) = 1 − ( 1 − p ) G − p G , u(p)=1-(1-p)^{G}-p^{G}, (1) which increases as p p approaches 1 2 \tfrac{1}{2} from either side and is approximately G ​ p Gp when p p is small (Proposition 1 ). On a task the student rarely solves, a scaffold makes some rollouts succeed, so the group contains both outcomes and the task can generate training signal. Therefore, a scaffold that helped earlier may no longer help the student learn. Our ablation study further illustrates the limitations of fixed guidance: using Skill0’s published skill bank as a fixed scaffold yields an ALFWorld success rate 15.3 points below AutoScaffold and 8.1 points below the RL baseline (Section 4.3 ).

blocks.en: A student may fail for two reasons: it may lack a strategy that a whole class of tasks requires, or a particular task may remain too hard for it even with such a strategy. Following the principle that support should match the capability that the learner currently lacks ( Wood et al., 1976 ) , AutoScaffold provides scaffolds at two corresponding levels. To define the first level, we group training tasks into classes using the categories that each training dataset already provides, such as the six task types of ALFWorld or the training sources of search-based QA, in the same way that SkillRL and Skill0 organize skills by task category ( Xia et al., 2026 ; Lu et al., 2026 ) ; when a dataset has no such categories, all its tasks form a single class. We write C ⁡ ( x ) C(x) for the class of task x x , and Section 4.1 lists the classes of each domain. • Class-level scaffolds S class ​ [ C ] S_{\text{class}}[C] capture strategies shared by the tasks in class C C , such as workflows (e.g., the order of steps that a type of household task requires), mistakes to avoid (e.g., moving an object again after it has been placed), and checks before finishing (e.g., confirming that the final answer is the quantity the problem asks for). Like the category-specific skills of SkillRL and Skill0, they transfer across tasks of the same class. By raising the success rate of a class, they increase the learning signal that the class provides, as long as they do not push its success rate far above one half (Proposition 3 ). • Instance-level scaffolds S inst ​ [ x ] S_{\text{inst}}[x] give support specific to a single task x x , such as a hint about its key step, an intermediate result, or part of its reference solution. One example is the solution prefix used by QuestA ( Li et al., 2026a ) , which reveals the first r x r_{x} fraction of the reference solution; our math experiments use this form. Such scaffolds mainly help tasks that the student cannot solve even with a class-level strategy: they let these tasks produce successful rollouts and thus contribute to training at all (Proposition 4 ). The two levels are complementary: class-level scaffolds move tasks that the student can already partially solve toward a success rate near one half, where they give the most learning signal, while instance-level scaffolds bring tasks with zero success into training (Appendix A ).

blocks.en: AutoScaffold updates the scaffold every K K RL training steps. We call each such period a block : the scaffold stays fixed within a block, and at the end of block k k a frozen teacher LLM updates it for block k + 1 k+1 (Figure 3 (b)). Training starts with no class-level scaffold, so every class-level scaffold the student sees is written by the teacher. The teacher makes all scaffold decisions; its instructions contain no domain-specific rules and differ across domains only in a short description of the task domain and the list of classes. The teacher may see reference answers of training tasks but never sees evaluation tasks. Each update takes four steps: gathering evidence, proposing edits, validating class-level scaffolds, and deploying the update. Algorithm 2 summarizes one update.

blocks.en: Since no human diagnoses the student, the teacher must find out on its own why the student fails, and which evidence answers this is not known in advance. A low success rate in a class may come from one shared mistake or from several unrelated ones; telling them apart requires reading trajectories, comparing failed attempts with successful ones on the same task, and checking whether a pattern seen in one trajectory recurs across the class. Unlike prior methods, which give the teacher a fixed sample of failures, AutoScaffold lets the teacher decide what to read. The teacher accesses the training log of the current block through three query tools, each returning a view of the log at a different level of detail: • Class statistics. Q stat Q_{\text{stat}} returns each class’s success rates with and without its class-level scaffold, and the numbers of tasks whose rollouts all failed or all succeeded. • Individual trajectories. Q traj Q_{\text{traj}} returns trajectories filtered by class and outcome. • Rollout groups. Q group Q_{\text{group}} returns all G G attempts on one task, showing how successful and failed attempts on the same task differ. The teacher gathers evidence in a multi-turn loop. At each turn, it either calls one tool, whose response is appended to its context, or stops and proposes edits. Starting from initial evidence, such as each class’s success rate on its held-out tasks V C V_{C} (described below) with and without the current scaffold, it chooses which trajectories or groups to read next based on what it has already seen; each response is kept within its context, and the teacher must stop after B B calls. The log of one block, however, shows only how the student behaves now, not how it responded to the teacher’s earlier edits. The teacher therefore keeps a memory M M of its past diagnoses and decisions, and can query M M for its latest three decisions to judge whether those edits helped. For example, at step 40 on ALFWorld, the teacher first calls Q stat Q_{\text{stat}} , finds that Pick2, Look, and Heat are the weakest classes, then calls Q traj Q_{\text{traj}} to read four all-failure trajectories from each of them, and finally reads its last three decisions from memory (Figure 4 , top). Replacing the query tools and memory with a fixed sample of failed trajectories, as in SkillRL, lowers ALFWorld success by 8.6 points (Section 4.3 ).

The teacher adds, revises, or removes S class ​ [ C ] S_{\text{class}}[C] to address a weakness shared across class C C . It writes these scaffolds as general strategies rather than answers to specific tasks. For example, after observing that the student in ALFWorld’s Pick2 class (two-object placement tasks) often places only one object, the teacher adds a strategy for finding and placing the second object (Section 4.4 ). • Injection frequency. The teacher sets q ⁡ [ C ] ∈ [ 0 , q max ] q[C]\in[0,q_{\max}] for each class, for example lowering q ⁡ [ C ] q[C] as the student succeeds in class C C without the scaffold. • Instance-level hints. The teacher writes or revises S inst ​ [ x ] S_{\text{inst}}[x] , or adjusts the fraction r x r_{x} of a verified reference solution shown to the student, giving more support to tasks the student keeps failing and less to tasks it can already solve. As a simple illustration, a hint for x 4 − 3 ​ x 2 + 1 = 0 x^{4}-3x^{2}+1=0 could suggest substituting t = x 2 t=x^{2} , leaving the student to solve the resulting quadratic and recover x x . Instead of domain-specific rules, the teacher’s instructions state two principles from the analysis in Section 3.1 , which hold in every domain. First, focus on classes with low success rates or many all-failure groups, where scaffolds add the most learning signal (Propositions 3 and 4 ). Second, reduce support as the student improves; for class-level scaffolds, start withdrawing once success without the scaffold exceeds 50%, a heuristic threshold motivated by our analysis (Propositions 1 and 3 ). The teacher may also leave the scaffold unchanged. Appendix B gives examples of its diagnoses and edits.

blocks.en: A class-level scaffold is inferred from a few trajectories, so it may fix the failures the teacher has read without helping other tasks in the same class. Because it is shown to the whole class for an entire block, a harmful scaffold affects many training steps. AutoScaffold therefore checks each proposed class-level scaffold on the current student before deploying it: • Held-out tasks. Before training, we reserve a set of tasks V C V_{C} from the training data of each class and exclude them from training. At the start of each update, the current student is evaluated on V C V_{C} without a class-level scaffold and with the current one, and these success rates are part of the initial evidence. • Three conditions. The success rates on V C V_{C} without a class-level scaffold and with the current scaffold come from the evaluation at the start of the update. For each proposed scaffold, we additionally run the current student π θ k \pi_{\theta_{k}} , the checkpoint at the end of block k k , on V C V_{C} with the proposed scaffold, using n n rollouts per task and matched seeds. • Comparisons. The teacher receives the three success rates ( v C none v^{\text{none}}_{C} , v C cur v^{\text{cur}}_{C} , and v C new v^{\text{new}}_{C} in Algorithm 2 ). Comparing the proposed scaffold with the current one shows whether the edit improves on existing guidance; comparing either with no scaffold shows whether the student still benefits from support in this class. • Decision. Using these results and its diagnosis, the teacher adopts the proposed scaffold, keeps the current one, combines the two, or removes the scaffold of the class. A higher success rate under the scaffold is not by itself the goal: the teacher prefers scaffolds that help the student succeed while leaving meaningful work for it, and how often the student sees a scaffold is set separately by q ⁡ [ C ] q[C] . Without validation, ALFWorld success drops from 93.9% to 79.8%, below the RL baseline (Section 4.3 ). Instance-level scaffolds are not validated, since in our experiments they are prefixes of verified reference solutions rather than text written by the teacher.

blocks.en: 4 Experiments
blocks.zh: 4个实验

blocks.en: Our experiments test whether AutoScaffold delivers the three properties argued for in Section 1 . Automatic : without hand-written scaffolds or hand-designed schedules, does it improve the student’s performance without scaffolds over RL baselines, and is it competitive with methods built on human-designed scaffolds? Unified : does the same procedure work across domains with different task structures and RL algorithms? Section 4.2 answers both. Adaptive : does revising scaffolds during training matter, and how does the teacher design and adjust them as the student learns? Sections 4.3 and 4.4 answer this.
blocks.zh: 我们的实验测试AutoScaffold是否交付了第1节中论证的三个属性. 自动:没有手写脚手架或手设计时间表,是否在RL基线上改善学生的成绩,是否与人类设计的脚手架上的方法有竞争力? 统一 : 同一程序是否在任务结构和RL算法不同的域中工作? 第4.2节回答这两个问题。 适应性:在培训期间修订脚手架是否重要,教师在学生学习时如何设计和调整? 第4.3和4.4节对此作了答复。

blocks.en: 4.1 Experimental Setup
blocks.zh: 4.1 实验设置

blocks.en: Domains and tasks. We evaluate four domains with distinct task structures: ALFWorld , with six household task types (Pick, Look, Clean, Heat, Cool, Pick2) requiring planning and object interaction ( Shridhar et al., 2021 ) ; search-based QA , covering single-hop (NQ, TriviaQA, PopQA) and multi-hop questions (HotpotQA, 2Wiki, MuSiQue, Bamboogle) ( Kwiatkowski et al., 2019 ; Joshi et al., 2017 ; Mallen et al., 2023 ; Yang et al., 2018 ; Ho et al., 2020 ; Trivedi et al., 2022 ; Press et al., 2023 ) ; KernelBench , with GPU kernel tasks ranging from single operators to full networks ( Ouyang et al., 2025 ) ; and math reasoning , covering eight competition-level benchmarks ( Mathematical Association of America, 2024 ; Mathematical Association of America, 2025 ; Harvard-MIT Mathematics Tournament, 2025 ; Brown University Mathematical Olympiad, 2025 ; Mathematical Association of America, 2023 ; Lightman et al., 2023 ; Lewkowycz et al., 2022 ; He et al., 2024 ) . Task classes follow each training dataset: the six task types in ALFWorld, the two training sources (NQ and HotpotQA) in search-based QA, six kernel types in KernelBench, and a single class for math (Table 2 ). Appendix C provides details.

blocks.en: Baselines. We compare with three types of baselines: (i) training-free methods , which prompt the base model without any training; (ii) training without scaffolds , which train the student with the same task reward but no scaffold; and (iii) training with scaffolds , which add human-designed scaffolds, such as skills, hints, or partial solutions, to the student’s prompts during training.

For search-based QA , we compare with (ii) R1-Instruct, Search-R1 ( Jin et al., 2025 ) , ZeroSearch ( Sun et al., 2026 ) , StepSearch ( Wang et al., 2025 ) , and GiGPO; and (iii) SkillRL and Skill0, at both the same scale as our student and 7B.

blocks.en: Implementation. In all domains, the teacher is GPT-5.5 with default reasoning effort and uses the same instructions apart from the domain description and class list. Scaffold updates occur every K = 10 K=10 steps with q max = 0.5 q_{\max}=0.5 , and each update allows at most B = 15 B=15 teacher queries. The teacher writes class-level scaffolds in all domains, while instance-level scaffolds are used only for math. Students and RL algorithms follow prior work in each domain: GiGPO’s settings for ALFWorld and QA, with Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct and Qwen2.5-3B-Instruct; StitchCUDA’s rubric-based RL for KernelBench, with a Qwen3-8B student cold-started as in Dr. Kernel ( Liu et al., 2026 ) and 600 training tasks; and SAGE (Qwen3-4B-Instruct with GRPO) and QuestA (Nemotron-1.5B with DAPO) for math, using their official training data. Experiments use 4–8 H200 GPUs, and results are averaged over 3 independent runs. The teacher’s API cost is a few dollars per run (Appendix D ). We evaluate AutoScaffold without scaffolds , so the results measure the student’s own capability.

blocks.en: 4.2 Main Results
blocks.zh: 4.2 主要成果

blocks.en: Across the four domains, the same framework, with teacher instructions that differ only in the domain description and class list, improves over the corresponding RL baseline under four RL algorithms (GiGPO, rubric-based GRPO, GRPO, and DAPO) and five students. In every domain where scaffolding methods exist, it also matches or surpasses them, although it starts from no class-level scaffold and uses no hand-written scaffold or hand-designed schedule.
blocks.zh: 在整个四个领域,同一框架,教师指令仅在域名描述和类名列表上有所不同,在四个RL算法(GiGPO,以rumic为基础的GRPO,GRPO,和DAPO)和五个学生下,比相应的RL基线有所改进. 在有脚手架方法的每一个领域,它也匹配或超越了它们,虽然它从没有级脚手架开始,并且没有使用手写脚手架或手设计的时间表.

blocks.en: ALFWorld. AutoScaffold reaches 93.9% success, 7.2 points above GiGPO, and is best on five of the six task classes (Table 3 ). The largest gains are on Look (+19.7), Cool (+16.2), and Pick2 (+15.3), the three classes where GiGPO is weakest and successful rollouts are rarest. The 1.5B student also exceeds SkillRL (89.9%) and SkillC (90.6%), which use the larger Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct, and SkillRL additionally keeps its skills at evaluation.
blocks.zh: ALFWorld. AutoScafold成功率达到93.9%,比GIGPO高7.2分,在6个任务类别中的5个类别上表现最好(表3). 最大的收益是Look(+19.7)、Cool(+16.2)和Pick2(+15.3),这三个类别GiGPO最弱,成功推出最罕见。 1.5B的学生还超过了SkillRL(89.9%)和SkillC(90.6%),后者使用较大的Quen2.5-7B-Instruct,SkillRL还保留了自己的评价技能.

blocks.en: Search-based QA. AutoScaffold achieves 46.1% average exact match, 4.0 points above GiGPO, and is best among 3B models on six of seven benchmarks (Table 4 ). At the same scale, it exceeds SkillRL and Skill0 by 7.2 and 5.3 points, and it also surpasses 7B Skill0 (44.4%). Although training uses only NQ and HotpotQA, the gain over GiGPO on the five out-of-domain benchmarks (+4.1 on average) is as large as on the two in-domain ones (+3.8), so the scaffolds improve skills that transfer beyond the training data.
blocks.zh: 基于搜索的QA. 自动脚手架实现 46.1%的精确平均匹配率,高于GIGPO4.0分,在7个基准中的6个基准中,在3B模型中最好(表4)。 在同一尺度上,它以7.2分和5.3分超过了SkillRL和Skill0,同时也超过了7B Skill0(44.4%). 虽然训练只使用NQ和HotpotQA,但是在5个域外基准(平均+4.1)上,GIGPO的增益与两个域内基准(+3.8)的增益一样大,因此脚手架提高了超越训练数据转移的技能.

blocks.en: Mathematical reasoning. With Qwen3-4B-Instruct, AutoScaffold reaches 70.1% average accuracy, 1.4 points above GRPO, and is on par with SAGE (70.0%), the strongest scaffolding method, without SAGE’s hand-designed hint levels and scheduling rules (Table 5 ). Guidance does not help by default: LUFFY, which trains on off-policy reference traces, falls 5.2 points below the base model. With Nemotron-1.5B, AutoScaffold reaches 62.4%, 2.0 points above DAPO and 1.3 points above QuestA, using 350 training steps compared with QuestA’s 1,100, roughly one-third (Table 6 ). The 1.5B student also surpasses DeepSeek-R1-Distill-32B (58.1%).
blocks.zh: 数学推理. 使用Quen3-4B-指令,AutoScolfold达到了70.1%的平均精度,高于GRPO1.4分,并且与SAGE(70.0%)相当,这是最强的脚手架方法,没有SAGE的手工设计提示级别和调度规则(表5). 指导默认无济于事:在政策外参考痕迹上进行训练的LUFFY低于基准模型5.2分. 使用Nemotron-1.5B,自动脚手架达到62.4%,比DAPO高2.0分,比QuestA高1.3分,使用350个培训步骤,而QuestA为1,100个,约为三分之一(表6)。 1.5B的学生也超过了DeepSeek-R1-Distill-32B(58.1%).

blocks.en: GPU kernel generation. AutoScaffold improves all six KernelBench metrics over StitchCUDA (Table 7 ), raising correctness from 59% to 63% on Level 1 and from 50% to 54% on Level 2, and Level 2 Fast 1 from 20% to 25%. Gains on the full-network tasks of Level 3 are smaller (+1 point on both metrics). Since this domain uses rubric-based rather than binary rewards, these results also show that AutoScaffold is not limited to the binary-reward setting of our analysis.
blocks.zh: GPU内核生成. 自动脚手架在StitchCUDA(表7)上改进了所有6个Kernel Bench度量衡,将1级的正确度从59%提高到63%,2级从50%提高到54%;2级快取从20%提高到25%. 第三级全网络任务的收益较小(两个度量标准上加一分). 由于这个域使用基于rumic而不是二进制的奖励,这些结果也表明AutoScaffold并不限于我们分析的二进制奖励设置.

blocks.en: 4.3 Ablation Study
blocks.zh: 4.3 读取研究

blocks.en: We evaluate the contribution of AutoScaffold’s main design choices through ablations on ALFWorld with Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct (Table 8 ). Each of the four main designs matters: removing the query tools and memory, removing validation, fixing the scaffold, or always injecting it drops the student below the RL baseline, so the gains come from how scaffolds are designed and used rather than from extra guidance alone.
blocks.zh: 我们评价AutoScaffold主要设计选择的贡献, 四大设计中的每一个都涉及:去掉查询工具和内存,去掉验证,修补脚手架,或者总是将学生注射到RL基线以下,所以收益来自于脚手架的设计和使用方式,而不是仅仅从额外的指导中获取.

blocks.en: Query tools and memory. Replacing the query tools and memory with a fixed sample of failed trajectories and a single teacher call, as in SkillRL ( Xia et al., 2026 ) , lowers success to 85.3%. With a fixed sample of failures only, the teacher cannot compare failures with successes, look further when the sample is inconclusive, or check how the student responded to its earlier edits.
blocks.zh: 查询工具和记忆. 如SkillRL(Xia等,2026年)中,将查询工具和内存替换为固定样本的故障轨迹和单师呼叫,成功率降至85.3%. 只有固定的失败样本,老师不能将失败与成功进行比较,在样本无定论时更进一步找,或者检查学生如何回应其早期的编辑.

blocks.en: Scaffold validation. Deploying every proposal without validation causes the largest drop among teacher components, to 79.8%, 6.9 points below GiGPO. Because a class-level scaffold is shown to a whole class for an entire block, an unhelpful edit affects many updates before the teacher can revise it.
blocks.zh: 脚手架鉴定. 在未经验证的情况下部署每项提案,造成教师人数减少最多,降至79.8%,低于GIGPO6.9分。 由于一个班级脚手架被显示给整个班级用于一个整块,因此一个无益的编辑在老师修改之前会影响许多更新.

blocks.en: Static scaffolds. Using Skill0’s published ALFWorld skill bank ( Lu et al., 2026 ) as a fixed class-level scaffold lowers success to 78.6%, 15.3 points below AutoScaffold and 8.1 points below GiGPO. The bank was not built for this student and cannot change as the student’s failures change; Section 4.4 shows how much the teacher’s own scaffold changes over training.
blocks.zh: 静地脚手架. 使用Skill0所出版的ALFWorld技能库(Lu等,2026年)作为固定班级脚手架,成功率降至78.6%,比AutoScafold低出15.3分,比GIPO低出8.1分. 银行不是为这名学生建造的,无法随着学生失败的改变而改变;第4.4节显示教师自己的脚手架在训练上的变化。

blocks.en: Update interval K K . Updating every 5 or 20 steps gives 90.1% and 90.4%, both above GiGPO but below the default K = 10 K=10 . Shorter blocks give the teacher less evidence per update, while longer blocks let the scaffold lag behind the student; K = 10 K=10 also needs half as many teacher calls as K = 5 K=5 .
blocks.zh: 更新间隔 K K. 每5个或20个步骤的更新给出了90.1%和90.4%,两者都高于GIGPO,但低于默认K=10K=10. 更短的块让老师每次更新的证据较少,而更长的块让脚手架落后于学生;K = 10 K = 10同样需要教师调用的一半如K = 5 K = 5.

blocks.en: Injection probability. Injecting the class-level scaffold into every rollout group ( q max = 1 q_{\max}=1 ) lowers success to 86.0%, slightly below GiGPO, although the scaffold content is produced in the same way. The student then never practices without help, which it must do at evaluation (Section 3.1 ).
blocks.zh: 注射概率。 将分级脚手架注入每个推出组(q max = 1 q max }= 1)将成功率降低到86.0%,略低于GiGPO,尽管脚手架内容以同样方式出产. 然后,学生从不在没有帮助的情况下练习,在评估时必须这样做(第3.1节)。

blocks.en: 4.4 Analysis
blocks.zh: 4.4 分析

blocks.en: The ablations show that each design is needed. This section looks at what the teacher actually does with them. We first follow a single update in detail, then trace how the scaffold changes over a full run, test whether revisions help the student at the time they are made, compare the scaffolds the teacher writes in different domains, and finally follow how the teacher adjusts instance-level scaffolds in math.
blocks.zh: 浮雕显示每个设计都是需要的. 本节考察老师对他们的实际行为. 我们首先详细跟踪一个单一的更新,然后跟踪脚手架是如何在全跑道上变化的,测试修改是否帮助了学生,比较老师在不同领域写的脚手架,最后跟踪老师如何在数学中调整实例级脚手架.

blocks.en: Figure 4: One teacher update on ALFWorld (step 40). Top: the teacher queries tools and memory, then gathers evidence from class statistics, failed trajectories, and its own past decisions. It reads them and finds meaningful information for further diagnosis and edits. Bottom: it diagnoses a different failure in each class and responds with a matching edit: adding, rewriting, reducing, or omitting a scaffold.
blocks.zh: 图4:关于ALFWorld的一名教师最新情况(第40步)。 Top:教师查询工具和记忆,然后从班级统计中收集证据,失败的轨迹,以及自己的过去的决定. 它读取它们并找到有意义的信息供进一步诊断和编辑。 底部:它诊断出每个类中不同的失败,并以匹配的编辑响应:添加,重写,还原,或省略脚手架.

blocks.en: How the teacher decides at one update (ALFWorld, step 40). Figure 4 follows this update. The teacher checks class statistics with Q stat Q_{\text{stat}} , inspects four all-failure trajectories per weak class (Pick2, Look, and Heat) using Q traj Q_{\text{traj}} , and reviews its last three decisions in memory M M . Its decisions depend on the needs of each class. • Pick2. The student picks up the first object after placing it or never searches for the second. The teacher adds a strategy for finding and placing the second object. • Look. The student finds the object or lamp but fails to bring the object to the lamp. The teacher specifies taking the object to the desk lamp, using the lamp, and then examining the object. • Heat. Even with the existing scaffold, the student reheats or retrieves the object after placing it. The teacher rewrites the scaffold to emphasize placing the object once and stopping. • Clean. The student already succeeds often and gains little from the scaffold, so the teacher keeps its text but lowers its injection probability. • Cool and Pick. The teacher identifies no failure requiring a scaffold and provides no text. Before deployment, each proposed class-level scaffold is also validated on V C V_{C} . Appendix B.1 gives another case, from a separate run, that records the full process of one update: how the teacher gathers evidence, what it diagnoses and proposes, and how validation decides which scaffolds are adopted.

blocks.en: Why these scaffolds help the student learn. These decisions show how the teacher turns observed failures into useful guidance. For Look tasks, the scaffold adds the missing step of bringing the object to the lamp. By helping some rollouts succeed, the scaffold can turn an all-failure group into a mixed group with a useful learning signal. The scaffolds describe strategies that apply across tasks in a class, while leaving the student to select objects and carry out the actions. The teacher also adjusts its guidance based on the student’s response. It clarifies the Heat scaffold when the student repeats actions after placing the object and reduces support for Clean when the scaffold provides little additional benefit.
blocks.zh: 为什么这些脚手架帮助学生学习. 这些决定表明,教师如何将观察到的失败转化为有益的指导。 对于 Look 任务,脚手架增加了将对象带入灯口的缺失步骤. 通过帮助一些推广成功,脚手架可以将一个全失败的组变成一个带有有用的学习信号的混合组. 脚手架描述一个班级中跨任务应用的战略,同时让学生选择对象并进行动作. 老师也根据学生的回应调整指导. 它澄清了学生放置对象后重复动作时的热脚手架,并减少了脚手架几乎没有额外好处时对Clean的支持.

blocks.en: Figure 5: Scaffold changes over training on ALFWorld. Left: scaffold-free success (top) and mean class-level injection probability (bottom), with training divided into three stages. Right: what the teacher changed in each stage (+ add, ∼ \sim revise, − - remove, ↑ ⁣ ↓ \uparrow\downarrow raise or lower injection probability).
blocks.zh: 图5:脚手架与ALFWorld培训相比的变化。 左:无脚手架成功(上)和平均班级注射概率(下),训练分为三个阶段. 对:老师在每个阶段都改变了什么(+ 添加,\\ sim 修订,--去除,\\\\去除,\\\去除,或注射概率更低).

blocks.en: How the scaffold changes over a full run. Across training, the teacher adjusts both the content of each class’s scaffold and how often it is used. The ALFWorld run in Figure 5 illustrates three stages. • Stage 1 (steps 0–50). When success is low across most classes, the teacher writes procedures for two-object, examine-in-light, and heating tasks. The mean injection probability rises, giving the student more frequent support. • Stage 2 (steps 50–80). As success improves, the teacher removes the broad workflows and retains a targeted reminder to heat the specified object. The mean injection probability falls close to zero. • Stage 3 (steps 80–150). The teacher addresses remaining failures with specific reminders, such as using the lamp’s exact name in Look and leaving the first object where it was placed in Pick2. It raises the injection probability for the still-difficult Pick2 class. The support thus evolves from broad procedures to targeted fixes, with changes guided by each class’s training evidence. For comparison, Skill0 uses a withdrawal schedule fixed before training.
blocks.zh: 脚手架是如何在全程变化的. 在培训过程中,教师既要调整每个班级脚手架的内容,也要调整使用频率。 图5中的ALFWorld显示分为三个阶段。 • 第1阶段(0-50步)。 当大多数班级的成功率都很低时,教师会写出双对象、光检查和取暖任务的程序。 平均注射概率上升,使学生得到更频繁的支持. • 第2阶段(第50-80步)。 随着成功程度的提高,老师会去掉宽的工作流程并保留一个有针对性的提醒来给指定的对象加热. 平均注射概率接近于零. • 第3阶段(第80-150步)。 老师用具体的提醒来解决剩余的故障,例如使用Look中的灯的确切名称,并将第一个放置在Pick2中的对象留下. 它提高了仍然困难的Pick2类的注射概率. 因此,这种支持从广泛的程序演变成有针对性的解决办法,根据每一班的训练证据加以改变。 作为比较,Skill0使用训练前固定的退出时间表.

blocks.en: Do revisions help the student when they are made? We measure the effect of scaffold revisions while holding the starting student checkpoint and number of subsequent training steps fixed. At representative ALFWorld checkpoints between steps 20 and 80, we create three branches and train each for 20 additional steps using the updated scaffold (AutoScaffold), the previous scaffold kept fixed, or no scaffold (vanilla RL). The updated scaffold yields the highest success at every tested checkpoint (Figure 6 ). Its advantage over the previous scaffold shows that the revisions improve learning over the following 20 steps. Its advantage over vanilla RL shows that support remains useful at these checkpoints.
blocks.zh: 修改是否帮助学生进行? 我们测量脚手架修改的效果,同时保留开始的学生检查站和随后的培训步骤的数目。 在具有代表性的ALFWorld第20至80步之间的检查站,我们利用更新的脚手架(AutoScaffold),即以前的脚手架被固定,或者没有脚手架(vanilla RL),创建了3个分站,每个分站进行20个额外步骤的训练. 更新后的脚手架在每个经过测试的检查站取得了最高的成功(图6)。 其与前作"脚手架"相比的优势表明,修改后在以下20个步骤上改善了学习. 它对香草RL的优势表明,在这些检查站,支助仍然有用。

blocks.en: What scaffolds the teacher writes in different domains. The teacher adapts scaffold content to the failures observed in each domain. In ALFWorld, its guidance describes action sequences for household tasks. In math, its class-level notes target recurring errors in otherwise sound reasoning, such as stopping after an intermediate result or boxing a quantity other than the one the problem asks for (Appendix B.2 ).
blocks.zh: 老师在不同领域写的东西。 老师将脚手架内容适应每个领域观察到的故障. 在ALFWorld中,它的指导描述了家庭任务的行动序列. 在数学中,其类级注释针对其他合理推理中反复出现的出错,如在中间结果后停止或将问题要求的数量以外的数量打入(附录B.2.).

blocks.en: Figure 7: Solution-prefix ratios during math training (Nemotron-1.5B). Mean ratio across all training problems. AutoScaffold (red) adjusts each problem’s ratio using training evidence. QuestA (gray) switches from 50% to 25% at step 100.
blocks.zh: 图7:数学培训中的溶解-前缀比率(Nemotron-1.5B)。 所有培训问题的平均比率。 AutoScaffold(红色)利用训练证据调整每个问题的比例. QuestA(灰色)在100步从50%切换到25%.

blocks.en:
How the teacher adjusts solution hints in math. We also examine how the teacher adjusts instance-level hints during math training, where each hint reveals a fraction r x r_{x} of the problem’s reference solution (Figure 7 ). We initialize the hints with QuestA’s data ( Li et al., 2026a ) , in which each problem has a 50% or 25% solution prefix, mix both sets from the start, and let the teacher adjust the prefix ratios alongside class-level guidance. During the first 100 steps, the teacher reveals more of the reference solutions, raising the mean prefix ratio from 28.7% to 33.7%. The mean ratio then declines to 26.7% by the end of training; at step 100, for example, the teacher raises the prefixes of all-fail problems that still have room and lowers them for problems the student already solves (Appendix B.2 ).
Our instructions ask the teacher to reduce support for problems the student can already solve. The teacher determines the timing and amount of each adjustment from training evidence. QuestA follows a fixed schedule, using 50% prefixes for the first 100 steps and 25% thereafter. AutoScaffold begins withdrawing support near this scheduled switch and reaches a similar final mean ratio through adjustments to individual problems. Together with the ALFWorld results, this illustrates how the same framework adapts both class-level strategies and instance-level hints as the student learns.
blocks.zh:
老师如何调整数学中的解决方案提示. 我们还研究教师如何在数学训练中调整例级提示, 我们用QuestA的数据(Li et al., 2026a)初始化提示,其中每个问题都有一个50%或25%的解决方案前缀,从一开始就将两套组合起来,让老师与班级指导一起调整前缀比例. 在前100个步骤中,教师披露了更多的参考解决方案,将平均前缀比例从28.7%提高到33.7%。 然后,在培训结束时,平均比率降至26.7%;例如,在第100步,教师提高了仍然留有空间的全失败问题的前缀,并降低了学生已经解决的问题的前缀(附录B.2)。
我们的指示要求老师减少对学生已经解决的问题的支持. 教师根据培训证据确定每次调整的时间和金额。 查询 A遵循固定时间表,前100个步骤使用50%的前缀,之后使用25%后缀。 AutoScaffold开始在靠近这个预定开关的地方取出支持,并通过对单个问题的调整达到相近的最终平均比. 这与ALFWorld的成果一起,说明了同一个框架如何适应学生学习时的班级战略和例级提示.

blocks.en: 5 Conclusion
blocks.zh: 5 结论

blocks.en: We presented AutoScaffold , an AI-for-AI framework that uses a frozen teacher to turn a student’s RL training experience into adaptive guidance. The teacher gathers evidence through query tools and memory, designs class-level strategies and instance-level hints, and validates class-level proposals before use. It adjusts both the guidance and the amount of support as the student learns. Across four domains, the same procedure improves performance over the corresponding RL baselines under scaffold-free evaluation and is competitive with or surpasses methods built on human-designed scaffolds. The gains include both correctness and execution efficiency on GPU kernel generation. Ablations and controlled comparisons support the value of evidence gathering, validation, and scaffold adaptation. Future work includes reducing the cost of teacher interventions and characterizing when learning with scaffolds improves the student’s independent capabilities.
blocks.zh: 我们提出了AutoScaffold(自动脚手架), 老师通过查询工具和内存来收集证据,设计班级策略和例级提示,并在使用前验证班级建议. 它既会随着学生的学习调整指导,也会调整支持的金额. 在四个领域,同一程序提高了无脚手架评价下相应RL基线的性能,与人类设计的脚手架上的方法具有竞争力或超过这些方法。 收益包括GPU内核生成的正确性和执行效率. 疏解和有控制的比较支持了证据收集,验证和脚手架改造的价值. 今后的工作包括降低教师干预的费用,在与脚手架学习提高学生独立能力时进行定性。

The requirement p x S < 1 p_{x}^{S}<1 matters: a hint that reveals the complete solution makes every rollout succeed, so the group is again degenerate and contributes nothing. Propositions 3 and 4 thus formalize the complementary roles of the two scaffold levels: class-level scaffolds shift the difficulty of tasks the student can already attempt toward the high-signal regime, while instance-level scaffolds expand the set of tasks that contribute to training at all. This motivates using instance-level scaffolds mainly for tasks that remain at zero success under class-level scaffold, with hints that are partial rather than complete.

blocks.en: As in ALFWorld, the update follows the student’s current ability: where more of the same support can still help, the teacher gives more of it; where the student already succeeds, it gives less; and where the support cannot be increased further, it proposes a different kind of support.

blocks.en: Appendix C Evaluation Domains
blocks.zh: 附录C 评价 域名

blocks.en: We evaluate AutoScaffold on four domains that differ in task structure, interaction mode, and reward.
blocks.zh: 我们评价AutoScaffold在任务结构、互动模式和奖励方面的四个领域。

blocks.en: ALFWorld ( Shridhar et al., 2021 ) is a text-based household environment in which the agent completes long-horizon tasks through multi-step planning and object interaction. It defines six task types, each used as a task class for class-level scaffolds: Pick & Place (Pick), Examine in Light (Look), Clean & Place (Clean), Heat & Place (Heat), Cool & Place (Cool), and Pick Two & Place (Pick2). We evaluate on the standard 140-game test split; an episode succeeds if the task is completed within the environment’s step limit, and we report the success rate.
blocks.zh: ALFWorld(Shridhar等,2021年)是一种以文字为基础的家庭环境,在这种环境中,代理通过多步骤规划和对象交互完成长视距任务. 它定义了6个任务类型,每个类型都用作班级脚手架的任务类别: 选择位置( Pick) , 检查光( Look) , 清洁和地( Clean) , 热和地( Heat) , 凉和地( Col) , 选择 二和地( Pick2) 。 我们评价标准140游戏的测试分数;如果任务在环境的步数限度内完成,一个插曲就成功,我们报告成功率。

blocks.en: The model answers open-domain questions by interacting with a search tool, deciding when and what to query and how to combine the retrieved passages into a final answer. We train on NQ and HotpotQA and evaluate on three single-hop datasets, NQ ( Kwiatkowski et al., 2019 ) , TriviaQA ( Joshi et al., 2017 ) , and PopQA ( Mallen et al., 2023 ) , and four multi-hop datasets, HotpotQA ( Yang et al., 2018 ) , 2Wiki ( Ho et al., 2020 ) , MuSiQue ( Trivedi et al., 2022 ) , and Bamboogle ( Press et al., 2023 ) . NQ and HotpotQA are in-domain; the others are out-of-domain. Exact match (EM) is used as the reward and the evaluation metric.
blocks.zh: 模型通过与搜索工具互动,决定查询的时间和内容,以及如何将取回的段落合并为最终答案来解答开放域的问题. 我们在NQ和HotpotQA上进行训练,并评价了三个单跳数据集,即NQ(Kwiatkowski等,2019年),TriviaQA(Joshi等,2017年)和PopQA(Mallen等,2023年),以及四个多跳数据集,HotpotQA(Yang等,2018年),2Wiki(Ho等,2020年),MuSi Que (Trivedi等人, 2022年),和竹果 (新闻等,2023). NQ和HotpotQA为域内;其他为域外. 精确匹配(EM)被用作奖励和评价的衡量标准.

blocks.en: KernelBench ( Ouyang et al., 2025 ) asks the model to write GPU kernels that reproduce a reference PyTorch implementation and run faster than it. Level 1 contains 100 relatively simple tasks involving basic operators (e.g., matrix multiplication); Level 2 contains 100 medium-difficulty tasks composed of multi-step operator combinations; Level 3 contains 50 challenging tasks involving full network architectures (e.g., AlexNet). We train on a dataset of 600 kernel generation tasks. Correctness is verified against the reference output, and we report correctness and Fast 1 , the fraction of tasks with a correct kernel that is faster than the PyTorch reference. Speed is measured on H200.
blocks.zh: Kernel Bench (Ouyang等, 2025)要求模型写入GPU内核,以复制参考PyTorch执行并运行快于它. 1级包含100个相对简单的任务,涉及基本的操作员(如矩阵乘法);2级包含由多步操作员组合组成的100个中难度任务;3级包含50个挑战性的任务,涉及完整的网络架构(如AlexNet). 我们在600个内核生成任务的数据集上进行训练. 正确性根据参考输出进行校正,我们报告正确性和快取一号,这是有正确内核且比PyTorch参考更快的任务的一小部分. 速度在H200上测量.

blocks.en: The student performs multi-step reasoning and outputs a final answer, which is checked against the ground truth. We use eight competition-level benchmarks: the recent contests AIME 24 ( Mathematical Association of America, 2024 ) , AIME 25 ( Mathematical Association of America, 2025 ) , HMMT Feb 25 ( Harvard-MIT Mathematics Tournament, 2025 ) , and BRUMO 25 ( Brown University Mathematical Olympiad, 2025 ) , together with AMC 23 ( Mathematical Association of America, 2023 ) , MATH-500 ( Lightman et al., 2023 ) , Minerva Math ( Lewkowycz et al., 2022 ) , and OlympiadBench ( He et al., 2024 ) . Following the corresponding baselines, the Qwen3-4B-Instruct setting (following SAGE) reports AIME 24/25, AMC 23, MATH-500, Minerva Math, and OlympiadBench (Table 5 ), and the Nemotron-1.5B setting (following QuestA) reports AIME 24/25, HMMT Feb 25, OlympiadBench, and BRUMO 25 (Table 6 ). We follow the evaluation settings of each baseline’s paper.
blocks.zh: 学生进行多步推理,并给出一个最终答案,根据地面真相加以检查。 我们使用八个竞争层面的基准: 最近的比赛有:AIME 24(美国数学协会,2024年),AIME 25(美国数学协会,2025年),HMMT 二月二十五(哈佛-麻省理工大学数学巡回赛,2025年)和BRUMO 25(布朗大学数学奥林匹克,2025年),以及AMC 23(美国数学协会,2023年),MATH-500(Lightman等,2023年),Minerva Math(Lewkowycz等,2022年)和Olympiad Bench(He等,2024年). 根据相应的基线,Quen3-4B-指令设置(按照SAGE)报告AIME 24/25、AMC 23、MATH-500、Minerva Math和Olympiad Bench(表5),Nemotron-1.5B设置(按照QuestA)报告AIME 24/25、HMMT 二月二十五、Olympiad Bench和BRUMO 25(表6)。 我们遵循每个基线文件的评价设置。
